 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. There are eight games left for the New York Giants, and they're not going to be easy.
 The Giants still hold their own destiny to win the NFC East for the first time since 2011. But here's a look at the Giants' most, and least winnable games the rest of the way.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 1. Week 12 at Colts (11/29/26)
 The Giants' next four weeks are a gauntlet, but luckily their most winnable game is right in the middle of it. Indianapolis is 3-7 and has sold off many of its top players like DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.
 Plus, former Giants quarterback Daniel Jones (59.6 completion%, 7 touchdowns, 12 interceptions) leads the NFL in picks through 10 weeks. Running back Jonathan Taylor is always capable of going off, but the Giants offense could put up points against Indy's 26th-ranked defense which has allowed the fifth-most points per game in the league.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 2. Week 18 vs. Eagles (1/9 or 1/10/2027)
 The good news is the Giants will close their 2026 season with one of their most winnable games. Sure, the Eagles are bound to put up a fight, especially if that game would wreck the Giants' season, but who knows what shape Philadelphia will be in, especially with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season.
 3. Week 15 vs. Browns (12/20/26)
 Todd Monken's Browns are essentially the AFC's Giants this season, starting 6-4 and sitting as a likely playoff team in mid-November.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But the Browns have been shoddy away from Lake Erie, sporting a 2-4 road record this season. Cleveland has already lost at MetLife Stadium this season, falling 17-12 to the Jets in an ugly game Oct. 11.
 You'd have to think John Harbaugh would know how to coach the Giants to beat Monken, who was Harbaugh's offensive coordinator in Baltimore the past three seasons. Plus, if Deshaun Watson is the quarterback, he'd likely be a sitting duck against the Giants' pass rush.
 4. Week 17 at Cowboys (1/3/27)
 The Giants beat the Cowboys in Week 1, and they haven't swept Dallas in a season since 2016. But Dallas (4-6) has underachieved, especially at AT&T Stadium where it is 1-3 this season and 5-6-1 in two seasons under coach Brian Schottenheimer.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement J.J. McCarthy already has a win at Jerry World under his belt, when as a member of the Minnesota Vikings he threw for 250 yards and two touchdowns and ran for one in a 34-26 win over the Cowboys last year. If the Giants can clinch the division in Dallas, the chances are good fans will take over the building, as well.
 5. Week 16 at Lions (12/27/26)
 The Lions are rolling on both sides of the ball, but they have been susceptible to opposing air attacks throughout this season. Plus, McCarthy went to Detroit and won last season, and the Giants nearly defeated the Lions at Ford Field with Jameis Winston playing quarterback a season ago.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Giants may be a heavy underdog in this game. Winning outright might be tough, especially in prime time. But the Giants should put up a fight.
 6. Week 14 at Seahawks (12/13/26)
 Giants fans old enough to remember 2005 should know that going to Seattle and winning is a tall order, especially against the reigning world champions.
 The Giants did win 29-20 at Lumen Field the last time they played there on Oct. 6, 2024. But Seattle is trying to get into the NFC playoff field and may have quarterback Sam Darnold back by then.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 7. Week 11 vs. Jaguars (11/22/26)
 Giants fans had better bring the energy Sunday. Jacksonville is 7-2 and looks like a bona fide Super Bowl contender, since it leads the NFL in point differential (plus-125) and has won three straight by a combined score of 115-40.
 So why isn't this the most difficult game on the Giants' docket? Because the Giants can probably put up yards against the Jags' 19th-ranked pass defense.
 8. Week 13 vs. 49ers (12/6/26)
 The Niners are 8-1 and lead the NFC, but they also have dominated the Giants in recent years. San Francisco has won three straight in this series, with each win coming by double digits.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Niners lead the league in offense and are third in the NFL in rushing offense, which makes them a matchup nightmare for the Giants, who are 19th in the league in run defense. Can the Giants put up points on the Niners defense the way the Cowboys did in their 46-40 loss Sunday? They'd better be able, or it could be a blowout.
